text:
Noah Patel: Dropping ADR draft for review: “ADR-0097 Runtime LTS branching & support window” (Confluence draft) https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=ADR-0097-draft

Main asks for #architecture:
- Branching model: `runtime-<major>.<minor>-lts` cut off a stable minor (first target `runtime-1.20-lts`)
- Support window: propose 12 months of patch support + 3 month overlap window between successive LTS lines
- Patch cadence: monthly (or ad-hoc for security/SEV1)
- Compatibility guarantees: API stable; “best effort” perf stability within SLO gates; no new features

Infra/security feedback especially welcome (branch protections, artifact provenance, EOL policy wording).

Connor O'Brien: +1 please be picky. We’re trying to keep this “enterprise readable” but still actionable. Also note: we’re trying to keep the release trains separate (normal runtime minor train continues every ~2 weeks).

Sahana Iyer: Read through. On branching: can we explicitly state what the “cut” point is? e.g. “branch is cut from the `runtime-v1.20.0` tag after a green CI run on `release/1.20`” vs “whenever we feel stable”.

Also branch protections: we should require status checks on the LTS branch that differ from main (GPU matrix + determinism check). If ADR says “same as main” it’ll be misleading.

Noah Patel: Yep good call. Right now it says “cut from the .0 release tag” but I didn’t specify the guardrails. I can add: cut only after:
- perf-canary baseline recorded
- Private installer RC validated against artifact
- security signing/provenance checks green

Marcus Lin: Security angle:
1) Support window language needs an explicit EOL definition. For enterprise audits, “12 months” isn’t enough; we need “after EOL, no patches, including security patches, unless contractually agreed (exception process)”.
2) Artifact provenance: if we’re calling it LTS, we need to commit to signed artifacts and verifiable provenance for every patch release.

Do we want to name the mechanism? If we’re doing cosign + provenance attestation, put it in ADR at least at a high level.

Connor O'Brien: Re: naming, ADR currently says “signed + attested” but doesn’t name cosign/SLSA explicitly. We can add “cosign signatures + SLSA provenance” as “current implementation” w/ caveat we may evolve.

Naomi Feldman: +1 to Marcus. Also want a sentence about vulnerability intake and embargoed fixes:
- security fixes can be patch-only in LTS without waiting for next monthly cadence
- comms are restricted until disclosure

Even if detailed workflow lives elsewhere, ADR should state LTS won’t be the “slow lane for security”.

Noah Patel: Makes sense. I’ll add “Security patches: out-of-band when required; subject to embargo handling; tracked via restricted channel; release notes may be redacted until disclosure.”

Sean Gallagher: From reliability standpoint: the “perf stability” language is a little hand-wavy. Can you tie it to gates?

Suggestion: “LTS patch releases must pass SRE-defined regression gates (p95/p99 latency deltas, error rate) on reference workloads before promotion.”

Even if thresholds are in the SRE doc, at least point to it.

Rafael Mendes: +1. Also please add what happens if gates fail: “hold patch”, “rollback”, “exception requires SRE approval”. Otherwise we’ll end up shipping because of schedule pressure.

Sahana Iyer: +1 to Sean/Rafael. Also if “cut from .0 tag” then we need to clarify what “.0” means. Is it the same artifact we ship on normal train? Or is there an “LTS .0” that gets rebuilt with extra steps?

If we rebuild, we need reproducible build story. If we don’t rebuild, we need to ensure .0 already meets signing/provenance requirements.

Connor O'Brien: Good catch. Current plan is: `.0` is a *new* build using LTS pipeline so it can include:
- reproducibility checks
- deterministic build verification
- signing + provenance

But source commit is the `runtime-v1.20.0` tag (no code delta). That should be stated.

Marcus Lin: If you do “rebuild from same source”, please be explicit about:
- what inputs are pinned (base image digest, compiler toolchain)
- how we publish SBOMs
- how auditors can verify “same source” claim

Even one line like “LTS artifacts are built from pinned inputs and publish SBOM + build provenance” helps.

Olga Petrov: From audit evidence perspective: ADR should explicitly call out traceability requirement: issue → PR → backport PR → tag → artifact digest.

If we don’t put that expectation in the ADR, teams treat it as optional later.

Mateo Alvarez: Read it end-to-end. Overall direction looks right.

One thing: 12 months support feels like the right starting point but we should acknowledge it’s “minimum standard” and can be extended for top-tier enterprise contracts (with an exception policy). Otherwise Sales/CS will promise random timelines.

Also “3 month overlap” — clarify whether overlap means both lines receive patches simultaneously or just “we will accept escalations”. I’d prefer “both lines receive patches” because that’s what customers interpret.

Noah Patel: +1. I’ll update overlap definition to “both receive patches” (assuming we can staff it) and add a statement: “extensions require exec sponsor + release eng + security signoff” so it’s not ad hoc.

Naomi Feldman: Another nit: compatibility guarantees should mention NVIDIA driver/CUDA expectations. Enterprises care about “will the LTS runtime still run on the same driver stack?”

Maybe: “No increases to minimum driver/CUDA requirements within an LTS line unless required for a security fix; such changes are flagged as high risk and require explicit approval + comms.”

Sahana Iyer: Strong +1. If we change base image/toolchain mid-line without calling it out, Private customers will get burned.

Connor O'Brien: Ok, capturing action items:
- define branch cut criteria + LTS `.0` rebuild semantics (same source tag, LTS pipeline)
- add EOL + extension exception policy language
- link perf/regression gates and failure handling (hold/rollback/exception)
- add explicit provenance/signing/SBOM commitment language
- clarify overlap = both lines patched
- mention driver/CUDA/min base image policy

Noah Patel: Thanks all. I’ll revise ADR today and re-post for final ✅ in this thread.

Marcus Lin: When you re-post, please tag me on the revised security/provenance section. I want to make sure we don’t over-promise (but also don’t under-spec).

Sean Gallagher: Same for regression gates section. I’ll sanity check it aligns with what SRE is drafting.

Noah Patel: Will do.
